commit_message:
openssl: when a session-ID is reused, skip OCSP stapling

Fixes #12399
Reported-by: Alexey Larikov
Closes #12418
pr_title: openssl: when a session-ID is reused, skip OCSP stapling

files.diff:
diff --git a/lib/vtls/vtls_int.h b/lib/vtls/vtls_int.h
index cc5a357180..af7ae552ed 100644
--- a/lib/vtls/vtls_int.h
+++ b/lib/vtls/vtls_int.h
@@ -73,10 +73,11 @@ struct ssl_connect_data {
   void *backend;                    /* vtls backend specific props */
   struct cf_call_data call_data;    /* data handle used in current call */
   struct curltime handshake_done;   /* time when handshake finished */
   int port;                         /* remote port at origin */
   BIT(use_alpn);                    /* if ALPN shall be used in handshake */
+  BIT(reused_session);              /* session-ID was reused for this */
 };
 
 
 #undef CF_CTX_CALL_DATA
 #define CF_CTX_CALL_DATA(cf)  \

fix_commit.author: Joshua Rogers
fix_commit.message: openssl: skip session resumption when verifystatus is set

location.description: New guard at the exact 2023 introducing revision.

findings.message: The new reused_session condition suppresses verifystatus, while the existing cache lookup can still offer a session when status verification is requested.

related_locations.description: Preexisting intro-era session-cache lookup must be disabled when verifystatus is set.

findings.suggestion: At this 2023 snapshot, add && !conn_config->verifystatus to the sessionid cache lookup so a full handshake and OCSP validation occur.
findings.title: Resumed OpenSSL session bypasses requested OCSP status check

ground_truth.root_cause: In the introducing tree, servercert skips verifystatus() when connssl->reused_session is true, but ossl_connect_step1 still loads a cached session under if(ssl_config->primary.sessionid). The 2025 fix gates a later cache_session API. The equivalent repair for the 2023 tree is the one-line intro-era guard if(ssl_config->primary.sessionid && !conn_config->verifystatus), forcing a full handshake and status check.
